question.text: Which of the following is TRUE regarding the selling of stolen, counterfeit or fraudulently issued securities under the PFUTP Regulations?

answer.text: It is exempt from PFUTP Regulations and covered only under criminal law
It is only prohibited if the securities are in physical form
It is not considered fraudulent if the person was a holder in due course or the securities were previously traded through a bonafide transaction
It is always considered a fraudulent trade practice regardless of circumstances

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the PFUTP Regulations (workbook pages 145-146), selling, dealing in, or pledging stolen, counterfeit, or fraudulently issued securities can be excluded from manipulative/fraudulent/unfair treatment if the person was a holder in due course or the securities were previously traded on the market through a bonafide transaction. The Trap: Option A ignores the explicit holder-in-due-course/bonafide-transaction exception in the regulation. Option B is wrong because the regulation does not distinguish between physical and dematerialized form for this exception; it is the bonafide nature of the prior transaction that matters. Note: 'Holder in due course' protects a person who acquired the securities in good faith and for value through a bonafide market transaction.
